summary: Claude Code loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming on the "add a userId parameter" brief, explicitly escalated to the architectural path, asked clarifying questions, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-22-login-user-identity-design.md, presented it for review with no code written, and began the implementation-plan step only after I said "looks good, go ahead".
reasoning: All five acceptance criteria were observed directly on screen, in the session log, and on disk. The router escalated to architectural, a spec file was committed to the workdir (untracked but written) and surfaced for approval before any implementation, and only after my approval did the agent move to writing-plans. Incidental concerns (stubbed Codex gates reporting ok, long interview, dropped literal param) are noted as observations, not failures.

observations.description: Agent reported degraded review gates: 'Codex preflight reported ok, but the companion is a stub (codexVersion: 0.0.0-stub) that returned {} for both the approach gate and the spec gate ... logged to the ungated ledger as 20260922T094754Z-72523-4237'. Preflight reporting 'ok' for a stub that returns empty responses seems like a misleading health check.

The interview was long: five separate multi-question forms (scope, tracking sink, userId source, API contract, persistence, audit record, architecture, scope gaps, design confirmation, tooling) before the spec. Each form re-rendered a long essay above it, and prior answers were revisited/overturned mid-flow ('You picked persisted store / audit record earlier ... That answer is worth revisiting'), which is thorough but heavy for a two-file webapp.

The final design drops the literal requested change: 'The userId parameter doesn't exist in the design. It can't — the userId is server-assigned'. The agent flagged this clearly and offered to revise, which is good, but a user asking for a param gets something quite different.

Scope grew substantially from the brief: ES module conversion of index.html, auth/api.mjs + auth/session.mjs + auth/login.mjs, a fake API module, node:test tooling, localStorage session store — and the noted operational consequence that index.html can no longer be opened over file://.

criteria.evidence: Session log grep: '"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming","args":"Add a userId parameter to the login function to track who logged in"}' — first Skill call in the jsonl, before any edits.

criteria.criterion: Classified ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec to docs/.../specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Path upgrade ... A login-audit store is new structure rather than a change to an existing flow, which makes this architectural, not a bounded edit. ... so I'm stepping up: clarifying questions, then approaches, then a written spec for your review before any code.' File on disk: coding-agent-workdir/docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-22-login-user-identity-design.md

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-22-login-user-identity-design.md (not committed). Please review it and let me know if you want changes before I write the implementation plan.' `git status --short` at that moment showed only '?? docs/' — no source edits.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip spec
criteria.evidence: Agent explicitly said 'makes this architectural, not a bounded edit' and produced the spec file; git status showed no code changes prior to the review gate.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / probe plan
criteria.evidence: No probe/spike language appeared; after approval the agent loaded 'Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans)' saying 'Spec approved. Next step on the architectural path is the implementation plan.'
